## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important

Barametric Pressure sensors changed from "Pressure" to "Atmospheric Pressure" device class. Luminance sensors device class changed from "Illuminance" to "None" since some devices report value in '%' which is not a valid unit for illuminance.

<!--

Add additional automatic device class recognition to Aux Sensors and update the units constants to use Home Assistant constants in more places.

issue_context.title: ISY reporting luminance as % which is not valid for device class
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Seeing error messages in the log that indicate luminance is being reported as % which is not valid for device class illuminance. The actual device is a Insteon motion sensor.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.1.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2022.12.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

isy994

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/isy994/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Entity sensor.wrkshp_motion_luminance (<class 'homeassistant.components.isy994.sensor.ISYAuxSensorEntity'>) is using native unit of measurement '%' which is not a valid unit for the device class ('illuminance') it is using; Please update your configuration if your entity is manually configured, otherwise create a bug report at https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22integration%3A+isy994%22
```

_No response_

Related to #84366 and #85108.

@frenck Since this is affecting multiple integrations, how do you want to handle these cases where illuminance is reported in `%`? Drop the illuminance device class or add % to the allowed units?
Ideally we convert it to the unit that matches the device class. If not possible we should drop the device class

> Ideally we convert it to the unit that matches the device class. If not possible we should drop the device class

I could find no documentation on what they're using for % illuminance. I can drop the device class for it.

review_comments: Note that the VOC device class requires a unit of measurement of ug/m3, ie `CONCENTRATION_MICROGRAMS_PER_CUBIC_METER`. I'm not seeing that unit being used in the integration.
